title: Paper Signal
summary: Bright typography and concise evidence for explaining what a technology actually changes.

look: Use a paper ground, near-black type and one signal colour assigned to the claim or value that changes.
Give the support shot and hero shot different visual scales. Keep product screens in their own colours.
beat-sheet: Reveal a sentence in meaningful groups. Let its strongest word or verified number occupy a different scale.
A ground change can mark a new premise or result. Hold the proof long enough to read it at phone size.
build: Use registered type blocks with the pinned font pairing and accent. Use real capture or a sourced visual for a claim.
sound: Use restrained clicks or paper-like transients at meaningful reveals. Keep the reading hold quieter than the entrance.
critic: Can the viewer name the claim before the accent moves on? Does the proof explain what changed?
Check the accent's meaning and the distinction between argument and decoration.

choices: Choose the hook, cadence and conclusion from the brief. A sentence, screen action or figure can carry the signature moment.

title: Pale Tint App
summary: Soft environmental colour around a real, crisp product interface.

look: Keep the tint in the stage and preserve native interface colours. Use light to distinguish the device from its ground.
Give the visible product state enough area for the viewer to read its labels without squinting.
beat-sheet: Show a stable starting state, one meaningful action and its result wherever the brief needs proof.
Push in on the control the viewer needs. Widen when the result depends on more of the interface.
build: Use a recorded product surface or an approved device plate. Frame the portrait composition around its own reading target.
sound: Keep action cues small and specific. Leave enough space in the bed for product state changes and speech.
critic: Verify button labels, focus and outcome at playback size. Check that the staging helps the interface rather than hiding it.

choices: Choose the device treatment, hook and order from the product story. An isolated proof shot may use a tighter palette.

title: Warm Editorial
summary: Patient explanation with generous margins, warm paper tones and a small number of meaningful accents.

look: Pair an editorial headline with clearly legible supporting type. One colour may guide a term, figure or annotation.
Keep texture shallow enough that line drawings, quotations and source labels read clearly.
beat-sheet: Allow the camera to follow the explanation from idea through worked evidence. Hold labels while reasoning continues.
Use the marker or a change of scale when it clarifies a connection that the viewer is ready to make.
build: Choose proof illustrations from the script. Keep live source data and chart scales traceable to the original.
sound: Use an unhurried bed or room tone. Reserve marked sounds for an editorial change of thought.
critic: Read the labels at phone size. Check whether each change in layout clarifies the explanation.
Check that the pauses serve comprehension and leave speech intelligible.

choices: Choose through-line, metaphor, transitions and ending from the topic. Long holds are a tool for reading and emphasis.

title: Editorial Paper
summary: Page-like composition for quotations, examples and stories with an argument.

look: Build a publication-like hierarchy with margin, a primary item and room for its caption or source.
Let quotations, imagery and editorial explanation occupy distinct visual roles.
beat-sheet: Use reframing or a page-like cut to turn evidence into the next question. Give a new document time to register.
Keep a source or quotation still when the narration asks the viewer to compare details.
build: Use the paper texture and type pairing at a scale that survives a phone screen. Credit evidence near the item it supports.
sound: Keep physical page sounds sparse. Use ambience or silence to distinguish sourced passages from commentary.
critic: Can the viewer distinguish quotation, commentary and source? Does each crop preserve the evidence it presents?

choices: Choose which exhibit leads and how the argument develops. The film may leave the page for footage, a diagram or a wide hold.

title: Keynote Dark
summary: Controlled contrast, spatial reveals and room for one high-stakes product moment.

look: Place the subject in a motivated pool or edge of light. Give the silhouette and surface separate reads.
Keep the screen or key interface readable independent of the beauty lighting.
beat-sheet: Move camera or light when the audience learns something. Establish any feature before cutting to an isolated detail.
Give the most important product action a held frame after the reveal.
build: Use real product surfaces or approved plates. Use restrained depth of field so functional details survive.
sound: Build a short motif around the product action. Use a quiet lead-in to let the reveal's attack register.
critic: Can the viewer identify what was revealed and why it matters? Check darks, glare and screen readability.

choices: Choose reveal mechanism, framing and beat count from the product. The film can move between plain proof and spatial spectacle.

title: Luxury Serif
summary: Restrained material detail, informed typography and deliberate space for a premium object.

look: Give the surface finish, edge and weight separate visual evidence. Use a restrained serif and quiet supporting type.
Keep tonal spacing around the object. Reserve the accent for a meaningful material or brand detail.
beat-sheet: Give each camera move a reason such as a visible join, finish or scale. Hold before the viewer needs the next fact.
Use a detail-to-context cut when a close shot would otherwise make the object hard to place.
build: Use macro footage, an approved object plate or physical lighting. Check the real texture after compression.
sound: Use surface-specific contact sounds and a small musical palette. Leave quieter passages around tactile detail.
critic: Can the viewer tell the material and scale apart? Check that copy remains readable when the composition is reduced.

choices: Choose whether hand, environment or detail carries the story. Mood, tempo and amount of negative space may follow the material.

title: Brutalist Mono
summary: Hard-edged, word-led structure for technical subjects and direct editorial statements.

look: Use a plain ground, bold hierarchy and an exposed grid. Let a genuine code fragment or figure carry detail where useful.
beat-sheet: Cut to a distinct layout when the argument changes. Short bursts of words can lead to a clear hold on the consequence.
Keep monospace movement readable by changing one content unit at a time.
build: Choose one sharp entry gesture per sequence. Check Cyrillic glyphs and long identifiers in the target format.
sound: Use short dry clicks, cuts or low accents with meaningful action. Leave breathing room around dense text.
critic: Can the viewer read the complete argument at speed? Does the harsh geometry serve the topic?

choices: Pick the pace, typography density and punchline for the audience. A quiet evidentiary frame can follow louder type.

title: Playful Pop
summary: Clear, elastic shapes and active type for short formats with an accessible tone.

look: Use a bright figure-ground hierarchy. Give the focal shape room before adding a secondary reaction or caption.
beat-sheet: Let a spring show impact, response or weight. Resolve into a stable pose before the viewer needs to read.
Change scale, layout or action when moving to the next thought.
build: Keep captions out of the product and presenter safe zones. Test a heavy and a light object with clearly different movement.
sound: Time the strongest pop to a visible change. Keep softer responses lower in the mix and leave speech distinct.
critic: Check the visual lane for captions and faces. Can the viewer follow the action with sound off?

choices: Choose the comic timing and visual motif from the subject. Expressiveness can come from one small motion against a still frame.

title: Product UI Walkthrough
summary: Readable instruction through real UI states, a purposeful cursor and narration-led holds.

look: Show the actual product at the intended language and state. Keep frame treatment quiet and native UI legible.
beat-sheet: Tie focus and click to the named action. Hold the result while the viewer reads. Widen when the control's location matters.
Give portrait its own readable camera path around the relevant region.
build: Use the capture log and approved narration timing. Show enough surrounding UI for the viewer to find the control afterwards.
sound: Keep voice clear above the bed. Use restrained feedback sounds where the action needs confirmation.
critic: Verify the cursor, spoken instruction and actual result in order. Test label readability in each requested format.

choices: Choose the demonstration pace, when the viewer needs an overview and where a chapter should end.

title: Archive Evidence
summary: Original sources lead a documentary argument through attribution, contextual holds and precise detail.

look: Keep the original likeness of each document, photograph or recording. Show a concise source label beside the evidence.
beat-sheet: Show enough of the whole item to establish context. Move to a marked detail only when the next inference needs it.
Hold quoted text long enough to read it even if the narration moves on.
build: Use assets with recorded provenance and permitted use. Label reconstruction or interpretation visibly in the scene.
Crop with care around dates, signatures and contradictory evidence.
sound: Protect source sound when it carries evidence. Use a restrained bed and room tone around speech.
critic: Can the viewer distinguish original material from interpretation? Check the source, crop, quote and date together.

choices: Choose the sequence of exhibits, point of view and tempo from the investigation. The visuals can shift between documents and real footage.

title: Physical Data
summary: Make a quantity tangible through countable units and a frame of reference the viewer can trust.

look: Choose one visible unit for the quantity. Fix its scale, origin and legend before comparing values.
Use material, shadow and spacing to separate groups while keeping individual units countable.
beat-sheet: Change a count by adding or removing units. Land on an equivalent camera view for each comparison.
Give the viewer time to read the legend and verify the final quantity.
build: Use verified values and readable units. Keep a camera angle that preserves counts and expose the final label beside the evidence.
sound: Use restrained material contacts to show arrival and separation. Cue groups where per-unit sound would obscure speech.
critic: Can a viewer count or reconcile the groups with the labelled value? Check that camera perspective leaves quantities comparable.

choices: Choose the object metaphor, staging and tempo for the real quantity. Declare a proportional mapping when one object stands for several units.

title: Tactile Paper Motion
summary: Assembled sheets, fibres and cut edges for editorial and playful hand-made motion.

look: Use a small set of papers with distinct fibres and thickness. Anchor texture and shadows to each physical layer.
beat-sheet: Let the action use physical verbs such as place, peel, fold or overlap. Step material motion where it helps the medium read.
Keep the camera steady or smooth so stepped actions remain the clear signal.
build: Use the collage block in portrait. Compose landscape layers with paper-fibre and registered framing tools.
Keep the cut edge readable and check that texture follows the sheet during motion.
sound: Use quiet paper rustle, crease or contact under the main action. Allow a pause after the strongest material gesture.
critic: Can the viewer trace the edges and order of the layers? Check that texture and sound support the depicted action.

choices: Choose materials, number of layers, rhythm and sequence for the story. Selected artwork and text may stay still while paper moves.
